newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. has no evidence of foul play in Lebanon crash.
newsitem.headline: U.N. has no evidence of foul play in Lebanon crash.

text.p: The United Nations said on Thursday it had found no evidence of foul play in the helicopter crash that killed four Italian soldiers and one Irishman serving with U.N. troops in southern Lebanon.

"At this time we have no reason to think it was a suspicious cause," said U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard, adding that all U.N. helicopter operations had been suspended until investigations were completed on Wednesday's crash.
"Secretary-General Kofi Annan has informed the Security Council of this incident," he said. "He wishes to extend his deep condolences to the families of the victims."

The helicopter, carrying peacekeepers from UNIFIL, the U.N. Interim Force in Lebanon, crashed in the Bint Jbeil area inside Israel's occupation zone in southern Lebanon. The zone this week was the scene of heavy Israeli shelling against the Islamic movement, Hizbollah.
The 4,488-member UNIFIL force was established in 1978 to restore the Lebanese government's authority over the southern part of the country after an Israeli incursion against Palestinian guerrillas.

Israel, after withdrawing its troops following a 1982 invasion, retained a so-called security zone along the Lebanese side of the border, aided by allies on the South Lebanon Army militia, to block attacks against northern Israel.
In addition to soldiers from Italy and Ireland, the U.N. force has contingents from Fiji, Finland, France, Ghana, Nepal, Norway and Poland. Its commander is Polish Major-General Stanislaw Wozniak.
